reviews.text: Render is a decentralized GPU network for rendering and AI tasks, using the RNDR token. Launched in 2017, it has partnerships with artists and studios. In 2025, it's booming due to AI demand. The team is from OTOY. It’s useful for creators.

Render Network is a decentralized GPU compute platform. It connects users needing GPU power (for 3D rendering, AI training or other heavy GPU use cases) with people who provide unused GPUs. As of 2025, Render has become popular in both graphics and AI. It migrated to Solana for speed and has partnered with different tech companies (for example Nvidia, Magic Eden). It uses a burn-and-mint model, where clients “burn” RNDR to use GPU time, minting new tokens to providers. In actuality, over 60 million frames have been rendered and around 842k RNDR have been burned on Solana. Render can be defined as the Filecoin for GPU compute.

Render appears to be building a global GPU rendering network kind of like Airbnb for graphics cards. The concept is neat, especially with AI driving up GPU demand some forecasts call that a massive growth area. It’s decentralized, so in theory it could offer cheaper, more widely available rendering power than centralized clouds. However, competing with AWS Nvidia will be tough. It’s early stage, and I personally think of it as a specialized niche project until more mainstream demand materializes.

After checking out Render, my honest take is that it’s an interesting and unique platform, especially for those in need of GPU rendering power. It allows people to monetize unused GPU capacity and offers affordable rendering services to creators. The concept is solid, and it’s a great option for those who need rendering on demand without the cost of traditional cloud services. However, it’s still early days, and there are some questions about its scalability and how widely it’ll be adopted outside of niche markets like animation and 3D design. It’s definitely worth keeping an eye on, but there are still some risks involved.
